title: Bigard's unemployment claim and Joe Glaser's bookkeeper
summary: After leaving Armstrong Bigard could not collect until an investigation found Frenchy skimming, and he received about $1,500.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: -- thing, when I left Louis Armstrong and I went to get my unemployment and I put it in and because New York and California, at that time, you worked together, you know for unemployment, so when the -- you have to wait two weeks before you get it and so after two weeks I went over -- nothing for me, so I say, well maybe they didn't straighten out the -- the guys says fill out your thing for next week. So I fill it out -- fill them out for about 12 weeks and then, I'm not getting anything. So one day, what

is this business? So the guy says -- says let's go in the back he wanted to talk he left his cage and give it to somebody else. So we sat down and we talked and he says, well, New York says they haven't got anything on -- on you. So I said well that's funny, so I says, what do you mean they don't have anything? And I was telling him my case, you know, so that I didn't know that Frenchy was stealing all -- just little insignificant money every week, you know. So he says, look, he says, have you gotten your weekly receipts from your pay.

I say, yeah, I got everyone, which I did. Had all of them, so he says, okay, I'll tell you what I'll do for you. He said I'll call the head office downtown and they can have a date for you and you go down there and you tell them the whole bit. I said, okay, so they called me and then he said -- I forget the day, but he said you go on down there, he says, ask for Mr. So-and-so, and he'll take care of you.

So I went down there with all my receipts, he said take all your receipts, took all of them. I went down there and he even had the deduction for unemployment and social security and all that, so this fellow down there, we started talking and he asked me for the receipts and I give him the whole bunch of them, he said, my God, what's all this? So he says -- says who's your boss? I said Joe Glager. He said who's Joe Glager? I said, Joe Glager's the one that owned the band. Say, well isn't Louis Armstrong the leader?

I say, yeah, he's just the leader, but he doesn't hire the band, he -- all he can do is fire them and he can't do that until he tells Joe Glager he don't want them. So that's the way they get fired. He said, but he's the leader, why, what -- so he says why isn't his name on here? He's the leader -- I say I don't know. He said we'll find out, so they got a disc and they're talking and I'm telling them all this so they said, okay, you'll hear from us.

So about two weeks later I don't hear anything and then I get a letter and it says you don't have anything to claim because they don't have a record of your payment. So I say, well somebody's got the record of the payment. So, this guy, he is flabbergasted, he said, dammit, there's something wrong. So what he did he must've sent somebody back, he said, so he had the people in New York to confiscate Glager's books and that's the worse [stink] thing that ever could've happened, because he is a stickler for government you know, Glager is, he really is. And they found out that Frenchy was stealing just a little drab of money -- well he fired Frenchy, and then they sent me a check for about $1,500.00 or something like that, can you imagine that?
